label: Human Enemy HP
rationale: Makes human enemies tougher or easier to kill. This changes their health, not their attack damage.
interaction: Weapon Damage affects the same time-to-kill from the opposite side. Raising enemy health while lowering your weapon damage compounds the effect.

label: Enemy Gun Damage
rationale: Changes how much damage you take from human enemy gunfire. Mutants and explosions are separate.
interaction: Human Enemy HP controls how long enemies survive; this controls how dangerous their shots are. Repeated-Hit Protection can also affect how sustained incoming fire feels.

label: Explosion Damage
rationale: Makes explosions more or less deadly, including grenade blasts.
interaction: Each explosion still has its own base damage. This setting scales the difficulty layer applied on top of those base values.

label: Weapon Damage
rationale: Changes the damage your weapons deal on a normal hit. Headshots have a separate multiplier.
interaction: Headshot Damage adds another layer on headshots. Human Enemy HP also changes the final time-to-kill.

label: Headshot Damage
rationale: Makes your headshots more or less powerful. This multiplies the hit instead of adding a flat damage bonus.
logic: 1.0x is the normal multiplier. 2.0x doubles the headshot damage multiplier used by the selected Base Preset; it is not an additive extra-damage percentage.
interaction: Weapon Damage also affects the underlying hit. The headshot multiplier scales that hit; changing both settings compounds their effect.

label: Weapon Jam Rate
rationale: Changes how often worn weapons jam. Each weapon's condition still matters.
interaction: Weapon condition and each weapon's own jam behavior still matter. Use this to make jams generally more or less common.

label: Mutant Hit Damage
rationale: Changes the damage from mutant attacks when they hit you. Mutant health is separate.
interaction: Mutant Health controls how much damage they can absorb; this control changes only damage dealt to the player.

label: Peak Hit Protection
rationale: Sets the strongest protection against several hits in quick succession. Higher means more protection.
logic: Higher values give more protection against rapid hits; lower values make them harsher. The number is protection strength, not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
interaction: Minimum Hit Protection sets the weakest protection in the same repeated-hit system. Incoming gun damage is independent.

label: Minimum Hit Protection
rationale: Sets the weakest protection against several quick hits. Raising it makes sustained incoming fire less punishing.
logic: Higher values give more protection at the weak end; lower values make rapid hits harsher. This is not a literal damage-reduction percentage.
interaction: Peak Hit Protection sets the strongest protection in the same system. Incoming gun damage is independent.

label: Healed Damage Still Counts
rationale: Decides whether damage you've already healed still counts toward repeated-hit protection. Your healing amount stays unchanged.
logic: OFF matches Novice and Stalker. ON matches Veteran and Master. Healing always restores HP normally; this toggle only decides whether the healed portion is still remembered by the repeated-hit protection system.
interaction: Works with Minimum and Peak Hit Protection; healing always restores HP even when past hits remain counted.

label: Mutant Health
rationale: Makes Bloodsuckers tougher or weaker, including their Mist variant. Other mutants are adjusted separately.
interaction: Changes only this mutant family's health. Other combat settings remain independent.

label: Phantom Spawn Interval
rationale: Changes the wait between phantom spawn waves in affected Master Psy encounters. Shorter waits mean more frequent waves.
logic: Lower percentages mean new phantom waves can return sooner. Master uses 50% of the normal wait time; 100% represents no extra Master override.
interaction: Pair this with Psy Phantom Count: shorter waits plus more phantoms can make an encounter far more intense.

label: Psy Phantom Count
rationale: Changes how many phantoms appear per wave in affected Master Psy encounters. Their spawn timing is separate.
logic: 100% keeps the normal count. 200% matches vanilla Master and doubles the configured phantom count.
interaction: Phantom Spawn Interval changes how quickly another wave can happen; this setting changes the size of each wave.

label: Psy Phantoms Cause Bleeding
rationale: Lets phantoms in affected Master Psy encounters cause bleeding on top of their usual attacks.
logic: OFF keeps this extra bleeding rule disabled. ON matches the Master override.
interaction: Bleeding Severity and medical treatment determine how serious the extra bleeding becomes.

label: Psy Gear Damage
rationale: Affected Master Psy enemies wear down your equipment faster or slower. Direct HP damage is unchanged.
logic: 100% keeps normal durability damage. 200% matches vanilla Master and doubles this durability damage.
interaction: This does not change their direct health damage. Armor/helmet durability settings still affect how your gear wears overall.

label: Hunger Rate
rationale: Controls how quickly hunger builds up. Higher means you'll need food sooner.
interaction: Food Hunger Relief changes how much hunger each item removes. Hunger-state thresholds still decide when penalties apply.

label: Bread Hunger Relief
rationale: Eating bread removes this many hunger points.
logic: Higher means more hunger removed by that item. At zero it gives no normal hunger relief.
interaction: Hunger Rate controls how quickly hunger returns; food healing and special effects stay separate.

label: Sausage Hunger Relief
rationale: Eating sausage removes this many hunger points.
logic: Higher means more hunger removed by that item. At zero it gives no normal hunger relief.
interaction: Hunger Rate controls how quickly hunger returns; food healing and special effects stay separate.

label: Canned Food Hunger Relief
rationale: Eating canned food removes this many hunger points.
logic: Higher means more hunger removed by that item. At zero it gives no normal hunger relief.
interaction: Hunger Rate controls how quickly hunger returns; food healing and special effects stay separate.

label: Condensed Milk Hunger Relief
rationale: Condensed milk normally removes all 100 hunger points. Lowering this value makes each tin less filling.
logic: At zero, condensed milk stops relieving hunger. Higher settings remove more hunger until the 100-point meter is cleared.
interaction: Normal HP healing and Weird Kettle alternative effects stay separate.

label: Hunger Stamina Regen Loss
rationale: Changes how much moderate hunger slows stamina recovery. It does not make actions cost more stamina.
interaction: This modifies regeneration, not the direct stamina cost of sprinting, jumping or melee.

label: Severe Hunger Regen Loss
rationale: Changes how much severe hunger slows stamina recovery. Master starvation can add extra penalties.
interaction: Master Starvation Mechanics can add further stamina drain on top of this standard severe-hunger penalty.

label: Fatigue Rate
rationale: Controls how quickly you get tired. Higher means fatigue penalties and the need for sleep arrive sooner.
interaction: Vanilla fatigue states still decide when their penalties become active. Energy drinks can reduce accumulated fatigue separately.

label: Energy Drink Fatigue Relief
rationale: Changes how much fatigue energy drinks remove. It does not slow the normal buildup of fatigue.
logic: 100% keeps vanilla fatigue relief. 50% halves it, 200% doubles it, and 0% makes energy drinks provide no fatigue relief.
interaction: Fatigue Rate controls how quickly tiredness comes back. This changes the amount removed by ordinary and special Energy Drinks.

label: Water Stamina Gain
rationale: Sets how much stamina drinking Water restores immediately. Longer-lasting buffs are separate.
logic: 38% is the vanilla refill; set 0–100% of maximum stamina directly, subject to the game stamina cap.
interaction: This changes only the immediate refill. Water's regeneration and stamina-cost buffs use separate settings.

label: Water Buff Duration
rationale: Changes how long Water's stamina-saving effect lasts. Its shorter regeneration buff cannot outlast it.
logic: 1x restores the original 30-second stamina-cost effect; the separate regeneration control starts at its original 5 seconds and cannot outlast the main effect.
interaction: Water Instant Stamina Restore controls the immediate refill separately.

label: Energy Drink Regen Duration
rationale: Changes how long an Energy Drink's stamina regeneration lasts. Other drink effects are separate.
logic: 1x preserves 45 seconds of normal/Limited stamina regeneration. Separate 5s/-100% and 15s/-30% action-cost effect durations cannot exceed the main regeneration period.
interaction: Instant Stamina Restore and Energy Drink Fatigue Relief remain separate controls.

label: Vodka Effect Duration
rationale: Controls how long Vodka's temporary stamina penalty lasts. Radiation removal is separate.
logic: 1x keeps the 20 s vanilla stamina-drain penalty.
interaction: Radiation removal strength is controlled separately by Alcohol Radiation Removal.

label: Beer Effect Duration
rationale: Controls how long Beer's temporary stamina penalty lasts. Radiation removal is separate.
logic: 1x keeps the 20 s vanilla stamina-drain penalty.
interaction: Radiation removal strength is controlled separately by Alcohol Radiation Removal.

label: Magic Vodka Effect Duration
rationale: Changes how long Magic Vodka protects you against Psy effects.
logic: 1x keeps the 90 s vanilla psi-protection duration.
interaction: This is a quest/special consumable and does not participate in ordinary Alcohol Radiation Removal.

label: Beer Strength
rationale: Controls how much a single Beer raises intoxication. Stronger drinks reach drunkenness stages sooner.
logic: Vanilla is 15 Drunkness per Beer. Against the current Medium 30 / Strong 80 stage boundaries, back-to-back vanilla Beer reaches Medium on the 2nd drink and Strong on the 6th.
interaction: Always visible beside Vodka Strength. Moving it updates Beer strength, the Beer Strong-stage drink count, and the back-to-back progression immediately.

label: Vodka Strength
rationale: Controls how much a single Vodka raises intoxication. Stronger drinks reach drunkenness stages sooner.
logic: Vanilla is 30 Drunkness per Vodka. Against the current Medium 30 / Strong 80 stage boundaries, the 1st vodka reaches Medium and the 3rd reaches Strong in the back-to-back preview.
interaction: Always visible beside Beer Strength. Moving it updates Vodka strength, the Vodka Strong-stage drink count, and the back-to-back progression immediately.

label: Sleep Threshold
rationale: Sets how tired you must be before you can sleep. Other conditions may still block sleep.
logic: Higher values require more accumulated sleepiness before sleep becomes available; lower values allow sleeping earlier.
interaction: Separate no-sleep effects from hunger, bleeding, radiation or Psy can still block sleep regardless of this threshold.

label: Minimum Sleep
rationale: Sets the shortest allowed sleep. It does not directly change how much HP or stamina sleep restores.
interaction: This is a time requirement, not a direct setting for how much each restorative effect heals.

label: Radiation Accumulation
rationale: Controls how quickly radiation builds up during exposure. Radiation damage and recovery are separate.
interaction: Radiation Recovery controls passive reduction separately. Master Radiation Mechanics can also add a stamina penalty at high radiation.

label: Radiation Recovery
rationale: Controls how quickly accumulated radiation fades on its own. It does not reduce incoming exposure.
interaction: This acts on recovery, not exposure strength. Radiation Accumulation determines how quickly new radiation is gained.

label: Radiation Damage
rationale: Changes HP damage once radiation becomes harmful. The danger thresholds do not move.
logic: 100% keeps vanilla radiation damage. 50% halves it, 200% doubles it, 600% multiplies it by six, and 1000% multiplies it by ten. Original stage thresholds stay vanilla.
interaction: Exposure determines how fast radiation builds up; recovery and Anti-Rad remove it. This setting only changes HP loss once radiation hurts.

label: Bleeding Severity
rationale: Changes how strong bleeding effects are when inflicted. The HP damage of each bleeding stage is separate.
logic: Higher values make bleeding effects stronger overall; lower values soften them. Novice uses 25%, Stalker/Veteran 100%, and Master 150%.
interaction: Low / Medium / Severe Bleeding Damage decide how much HP you lose once each bleeding state is active. Natural Bleeding Recovery and medical treatment decide how quickly bleeding goes away.

label: Natural Bleeding Recovery
rationale: Controls how quickly bleeding fades without treatment. Bandages and medkits work separately.
interaction: Bandages and medkits apply direct bleeding removal independently of this passive rate.

label: Max Health
rationale: Changes your total HP. Healing strength and damage resistance stay separate.
interaction: The game keeps its vanilla low-health state boundary. Other systems may also assume a 100-point health scale, so very large Max Health changes should be tested in game.

label: Passive HP Regen
rationale: Controls whether your HP recovers slowly on its own. Zero keeps the original no-passive-healing behavior.
logic: Zero keeps vanilla behavior. Raising it adds passive healing over time.
interaction: Health Recovery Delay decides when recovery can begin. Other healing sources, such as low-health recovery and medkits, stay separate.

label: Regen Delay
rationale: Sets the wait before compatible HP recovery can start. It won't create healing if no recovery effect is active.
logic: Higher values postpone actor-level HP regeneration for longer; lower values shorten the configured delay.
interaction: If Passive HP Regen is set to 0, this delay may have no visible effect until another compatible health-recovery effect is active.

label: Health Regen Strength
rationale: Makes active HP recovery stronger or weaker. It does not start passive healing by itself.
logic: 100% keeps compatible regeneration effects at full strength. Lower values weaken them; higher values strengthen them. Vanilla uses 100% on Novice/Stalker, 75% on Veteran and 50% on Master.
interaction: Passive HP Regen is 0 in vanilla, so this matters mainly when another effect is already restoring health, such as low-health recovery.

label: Low-HP Recovery Rate
rationale: Changes the recovery speed of the game's normal low-health effect. Master penalties can reduce it.
interaction: Health Regen Strength can scale this effect, and the Master low-health penalty can reduce it further.

label: Master Low-HP Penalties
rationale: Enables the extra low-health penalty used on Master difficulty. Normal low-health recovery stays separate.
logic: OFF leaves only the normal low-health system. ON adds the extra Master recovery penalty whenever the game enters its Master low-health state.
interaction: The game keeps the vanilla activation point for this state. The child control only changes how strong the recovery penalty is.

label: Master Low-HP Regen Loss
rationale: Slows HP recovery while badly wounded when Master low-health penalties are enabled.
logic: Higher values suppress health regeneration more strongly; zero removes this penalty component.
interaction: This remains inactive while Master Low-HP Penalties is OFF. It layers on top of ordinary low-health recovery and the Health Regen Strength setting.

label: Healing Amount
rationale: Changes how much HP Bandages and the three Medkit types restore. Bleeding and radiation treatment stay separate.

label: Food Restores Health
rationale: Decides whether ordinary food can restore HP. Hunger relief and special food effects still work.
logic: ON keeps vanilla food healing. OFF removes healing from the supported food items.
interaction: Bandage healing remains controlled by the Healing Amount radar. Weird Kettle alternative food effects are deliberately outside this switch.

label: Master Bandage Healing
rationale: Changes how much a Bandage heals when Master consumable penalties are enabled.
logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Bandage heal less. With the untouched base heal of 20 HP, vanilla Master gives about 5.0 HP.
interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

label: Master Medkit Healing
rationale: Changes how much a regular Medkit heals when Master consumable penalties are enabled.
logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Medkit heal less. With the untouched base heal of 70 HP, vanilla Master gives about 49.7 HP.
interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

label: Master Army Medkit Healing
rationale: Changes how much an Army Medkit heals when Master consumable penalties are enabled.
logic: 100% means no Master healing penalty. Lower values make the Army Medkit heal less. With the untouched base heal of 85 HP, vanilla Master gives about 69.7 HP.
interaction: This setting only has an effect while Master Consumable Effect Penalties are ON. Changing both the base heal and this Master percentage compounds the result.

label: Bandage Bleed Removal
rationale: Changes how much bleeding a Bandage removes. Natural recovery is separate.
interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

label: Medkit Bleed Removal
rationale: Changes how much bleeding a regular Medkit removes. Its HP healing is separate.
interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

label: Army Medkit Bleed Removal
rationale: Changes how much bleeding an Army Medkit removes. Its HP healing is separate.
interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

label: Scientific Medkit Bleed Removal
rationale: Changes how much bleeding a Scientific Medkit removes. Its HP healing is separate.
interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Natural Bleeding Recovery and bleeding damage remain separate.

label: Scientific Medkit Radiation Removal
rationale: Changes how much radiation a Scientific Medkit removes. Its HP healing is separate.
interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Radiation build-up and natural radiation recovery remain separate.

label: Anti-Rad Radiation Removal
rationale: Changes how much radiation Anti-Rad removes when used.
interaction: This changes direct treatment only. Radiation build-up and natural radiation recovery remain separate.

label: Max Stamina
rationale: Changes your total stamina pool. Recovery speed and action costs stay separate.
interaction: Action costs are direct stamina values, so changing Maximum Stamina changes how many actions fit into a full bar even when their individual costs are untouched.

label: Vault Height
rationale: Changes the tallest obstacle you can vault over. Waist and eye-height markers are visual guides.
logic: Higher lets you vault taller obstacles; lower restricts vaulting. This changes height reach, not jump distance.
interaction: Vault stamina cost, landing rules and collision checks remain independent.

label: Medium-Water Stamina Drain
rationale: Changes the extra stamina spent while moving through medium-depth water.
logic: Higher percentages make movement actions consume more stamina while moderately immersed; lower values soften the water penalty.
interaction: This changes penalty strength only. Water immersion thresholds remain unchanged.

label: Deep-Water Stamina Drain
rationale: Changes the extra stamina spent while moving through deep water.
logic: Higher percentages make deep-water movement substantially more expensive; lower values reduce that stamina pressure.
interaction: This does not change the water-depth thresholds or the separate deadly-water instant-death effect.

label: Stamina Regen
rationale: Changes how fast stamina comes back. Sprinting and other action costs are separate.
interaction: Movement-state values, hunger penalties and fatigue effects can reduce this base regeneration in context.

label: Action Costs
rationale: Changes stamina spent sprinting, jumping, vaulting and using melee. Aiming instead has a separate recovery effect.

label: Maximum Carry Weight
rationale: Changes your normal carrying limit before weight penalties start.
interaction: Encumbrance thresholds and equipment-derived carry-weight bonuses can affect how the load feels before the absolute maximum is reached.

label: Extra Corpse Loot
rationale: Choose the extra loot package added to ordinary human corpses: Medicine + Ammo, Water, or None.
interaction: Normal corpse loot is generated separately. Extra Corpse Loot selects an additional package.

label: NPC Medical Drop Chance
rationale: Controls how often ordinary human enemies carry medical items. Stack sizes are separate.
logic: 0-200% changes the vanilla medical drop chance. 50% halves it, 100% keeps vanilla, and 200% doubles it up to a maximum of 100%.
interaction: Affects ordinary human enemies only. It does not change zombies, named/story characters, traders, stash loot, or the amount inside each medical stack.

label: Bonus Ammo Drops
rationale: Changes the bonus ammo found on ordinary human corpses when Medicine + Ammo is selected. Loaded weapon ammo is unaffected.
logic: Higher gives more rounds in the extra Medicine + Ammo corpse package; zero removes those bonus ammo stacks. Loaded gun ammo does not change.
interaction: Extra Corpse Loot must be set to Medicine + Ammo. The game still limits calibers by enemy progression.

label: NPC Weapon Condition
rationale: Sets the minimum and maximum condition of weapons found on ordinary human enemies.
logic: Higher MIN improves the worst condition you can find. Higher MAX allows better-condition weapons; MIN cannot exceed MAX.
interaction: Changes only the condition of weapons dropped by ordinary human enemies. It does not change which weapons they use, their ammo, health, traders, zombies, or story characters.

label: Medical Stash Priority
rationale: Makes medical items more or less favored in eligible stash loot pools. This is priority, not a drop percentage.
logic: Higher priority favors medical loot against other eligible stash categories. Zero removes its relative weight where supported.
interaction: Priority does not raise original chance checks or bypass a stash's rank and loot restrictions.

label: Food Stash Priority
rationale: Makes food more or less favored in eligible stash loot pools. This is priority, not a drop percentage.
logic: Higher priority favors food against other eligible stash categories. Zero removes its relative weight where supported.
interaction: Priority does not raise original chance checks or bypass a stash's rank and loot restrictions.

label: Drinks Stash Priority
rationale: Makes drinks more or less favored in eligible stash loot pools. This is priority, not a drop percentage.
logic: Higher priority favors drinks against other eligible stash categories. Zero removes its relative weight where supported.
interaction: Priority does not raise original chance checks or bypass a stash's rank and loot restrictions.

label: Bandages Stash Priority
rationale: Changes how strongly Bandages compete for a place in eligible medical loot pools. Chance is separate.
logic: Higher priority favors Bandages relative to other supported medical loot. Zero excludes this type from the weighted selection.
interaction: The separate Bandage Chance Modifier still controls original chance rolls.

label: Bandage Chance Modifier
rationale: Scales the original chance for eligible Bandages. 100% keeps that chance, without changing priority.
logic: 100% keeps the original Bandage chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that chance roll. This is not a whole-stash drop rate.
interaction: Bandage priority or availability is separate; the stash's existing eligibility rules still apply.

label: Medkits Stash Priority
rationale: Changes how strongly Medkits compete for a place in eligible medical loot pools. Chance is separate.
logic: Higher priority favors Medkits relative to other supported medical loot. Zero excludes this type from the weighted selection.
interaction: The separate Medkit Chance Modifier still controls original chance rolls.

label: Medkit Chance Modifier
rationale: Scales the original chance for eligible Medkits. 100% keeps that chance, without changing priority.
logic: 100% keeps the original Medkit chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that chance roll. This is not a whole-stash drop rate.
interaction: Medkit priority or availability is separate; the stash's existing eligibility rules still apply.

label: Army Medkits Stash Priority
rationale: Changes how strongly Army Medkits compete for a place in eligible medical loot pools. Chance is separate.
logic: Higher priority favors Army Medkits relative to other supported medical loot. Zero excludes this type from the weighted selection.
interaction: The separate Army Medkit Chance Modifier still controls original chance rolls.

label: Army Medkit Chance Modifier
rationale: Scales the original chance for eligible Army Medkits. 100% keeps that chance, without changing priority.
logic: 100% keeps the original Army Medkit chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that chance roll. This is not a whole-stash drop rate.
interaction: Army Medkit priority or availability is separate; the stash's existing eligibility rules still apply.

label: Anti-Rad Availability
rationale: Enables or disables Anti-Rad entries in eligible medical stash loot pools. Drop chance is controlled separately.
logic: ON allows Anti-Rad in its eligible stash pool; OFF excludes it from that pool. The original chance check still applies.
interaction: Anti-Rad Chance Modifier scales the separate chance check while Anti-Rad is allowed.

label: Anti-Rad Chance Modifier
rationale: Scales the original chance for eligible Anti-Rad items. 100% keeps that chance.
logic: 100% keeps the original Anti-Rad chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that chance roll. This is not a whole-stash drop rate.
interaction: Anti-Rad priority or availability is separate; the stash's existing eligibility rules still apply.

label: Minimum Medkits
rationale: Sets the minimum number of Medkits in an eligible stack when that loot entry appears. It does not guarantee a drop.
logic: Raises or lowers the minimum Medkit stack size. Zero keeps the original minimum where the item is eligible.
interaction: Only stack size changes; chance checks and which stashes may contain this item stay separate.

label: Maximum Medkits
rationale: Sets the maximum number of Medkits in an eligible stack when that loot entry appears. Zero can exclude them.
logic: Caps the Medkit stack size. Zero excludes it from eligible stacks; five preserves the original supported maximum.
interaction: Only stack size changes; chance checks and which stashes may contain this item stay separate.

label: Minimum Army Medkits
rationale: Sets the minimum Army Medkits in an eligible stack when that loot entry appears. It does not guarantee a drop.
logic: Raises or lowers the minimum Army Medkit stack size. Zero keeps the original minimum where the item is eligible.
interaction: Only stack size changes; chance checks and which stashes may contain this item stay separate.

label: Maximum Army Medkits
rationale: Sets the maximum Army Medkits in an eligible stack when that loot entry appears. Zero can exclude them.
logic: Caps the Army Medkit stack size. Zero excludes it from eligible stacks; five preserves the original supported maximum.
interaction: Only stack size changes; chance checks and which stashes may contain this item stay separate.

label: Enable Extra Stash Gear
rationale: Adds optional progression gear to eligible regular stashes. Scripted, unique and quest rewards stay protected.
logic: ON enables extra, rank-appropriate gear in eligible stashes. OFF disables that bonus system.
interaction: The bonus system also replaces 13 verified regular-weapon stash placements. Quest and unique rewards remain protected.

label: Bonus Gear Coverage
rationale: Sets the share of eligible regular stash locations offered bonus gear. It is not the chance of getting an item.
logic: Higher covers more eligible stashes; zero covers none. Full coverage still does not guarantee an item.
interaction: Bonus Chance controls each offered item's roll; category priorities choose which gear can be offered.

label: Weapon Bonus Priority
rationale: Favors or discourages weapons as a bonus gear category. Zero removes weapons from that bonus mix.
logic: Higher priority favors weapons when a supported stash chooses its bonus gear types. Zero excludes this category.
interaction: Coverage decides which stashes participate; Bonus Chance checks each offered item. Rank limits still apply.

label: Armor Bonus Priority
rationale: Favors or discourages armor as a bonus gear category. Zero removes armor from that bonus mix.
logic: Higher priority favors armor when a supported stash chooses its bonus gear types. Zero excludes this category.
interaction: Coverage decides which stashes participate; Bonus Chance checks each offered item. Rank limits still apply.

label: Artifact Bonus Priority
rationale: Favors or discourages artifacts as a bonus gear category. Zero removes artifacts from that bonus mix.
logic: Higher priority favors artifacts when a supported stash chooses its bonus gear types. Zero excludes this category.
interaction: Coverage decides which stashes participate; Bonus Chance checks each offered item. Rank limits still apply.

label: Attachment Bonus Priority
rationale: Favors or discourages attachments as bonus gear. Only suitable progression tiers are used.
logic: Higher priority favors attachments when a supported stash chooses its bonus gear types. Zero excludes this category.
interaction: Coverage decides which stashes participate; Bonus Chance checks each offered item. Rank limits still apply.

label: Bonus Chance
rationale: Sets the chance check for each eligible bonus gear candidate. Even 100% does not guarantee gear in every stash.
logic: Higher improves the odds for each offered bonus item. Even 100% still needs an eligible stash and item candidate.
interaction: Use Bonus Gear Coverage for the number of eligible locations and category priority for the types of gear offered.

label: Basic Stash Ammo
rationale: Changes the number of rounds in eligible Basic, Standard and Rare stash ammo stacks together. Item selection stays separate.
interaction: One Ammo Quantity control changes eligible ammo stack sizes in Basic, Standard and Rare stashes together.

label: Basic Stash RGD-5 Grenade Chance
rationale: Changes the chance of an RGD-5 reward in an eligible Basic stash. Grenade quantity stays separate.
logic: 0% means Basic stashes never contain the RGD-5 from this setting. 10% is vanilla. 100% sets the native Basic RGD-5 chance when that eligible source branch is evaluated; it does not force every physical stash to contain grenades.
interaction: Pair it with Basic Stash RGD-5 Grenade Amount: Chance decides whether the grenade appears; Amount decides how many you get.

label: Basic Stash RGD-5 Grenade Amount
rationale: Changes how many RGD-5 grenades appear when the eligible Basic stash grenade reward succeeds.
logic: Choose an exact 0-4 grenades when the grenade entry is present. Vanilla is 1.
interaction: Chance and Amount are separate: 0% Chance means no grenade appears; Amount decides how many are given when it does.

label: Ammo per Box
rationale: Changes how many rounds breakable ammo boxes give you. Ammo type selection is separate.
logic: 50-200% changes how many rounds are found in breakable ammo boxes. 100% keeps vanilla amounts.
interaction: Works with Ammo Box Distribution: Amount changes how many rounds you get, while Distribution changes which ammo families appear more often.

label: Ammo Type Mix
rationale: Favors or discourages ammo types in breakable boxes. This changes the mix, not the number of rounds.
logic: Higher priority makes an ammo family more likely within supported box pools. 1× preserves the original mix.
interaction: Ammo per Box changes how many rounds appear, not which caliber families are favored.

label: Grenades per Box
rationale: Changes how many grenades come from breakable grenade boxes. Grenade type stays the same.
logic: 50-200% in 50% steps. Vanilla 1-2 becomes 1-1 at 50%, 1-2 at 100%, 2-3 at 150%, and 2-4 at 200%.
interaction: Changes grenade amounts in breakable grenade boxes only. Normal stashes, corpse loot, and NPC grenade loadouts are unaffected.

label: Standard Medical Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of medical items in Standard stashes. 100% keeps their original odds; it does not guarantee a drop.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Standard stash medical items only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Standard Drinks Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of drinks in Standard stashes. 100% keeps their original odds; it does not guarantee a drop.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Standard stash drinks only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Standard Coupon Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of coupons in Standard stashes. 100% keeps their original odds; it does not guarantee a payout.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Standard stash coupons only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Rare Ammo Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of ammo in Rare stashes. 100% keeps the original odds, not a guaranteed drop.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Rare stash ammo only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Rare Medical Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of medical items in Rare stashes. 100% keeps the original odds, not a guaranteed drop.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Rare stash medical items only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Rare Food Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of food in Rare stashes. 100% keeps the original odds, not a guaranteed drop.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Rare stash food only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Rare Drinks Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of drinks in Rare stashes. 100% keeps the original odds, not a guaranteed drop.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Rare stash drinks only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Rare Grenade Chance
rationale: Scales the original chance of grenades in Rare stashes. 100% keeps the original odds, not a guaranteed drop.
logic: 100% preserves each original item chance; 50% halves it and 0% disables that roll. This never guarantees a whole stash.
interaction: Affects eligible Rare stash grenades only. Availability, selection priority and stack size remain separate.

label: Rare Stash Coupon Chance
rationale: Changes the chance for coupon rewards in eligible Rare stashes. Reward size still depends on progression.
logic: Novice and Stalker use 20%; Veteran and Master use 10%. This setting only changes whether coupons can appear, not which Common, Rare, Epic or Legendary coupon tier is selected.
interaction: This is a chance for the eligible Rare coupon reward entry, not the chance to find a Rare stash or its reward tier.

label: Starting Coupons
rationale: Sets how many coupons you begin a new game with. It does not add money to existing saves.
interaction: This only changes the starting wallet for a new game. It does not add coupons to an existing save.

label: Prices Traders Pay
rationale: Changes the prices traders offer when you sell items. Their other pricing rules still apply.
logic: Higher raises what traders offer when you sell; lower reduces it. This is a price modifier, not an exact payout.
interaction: Broken Gear Value and item condition also affect what you can sell and for how much.

label: Prices You Pay
rationale: Changes the prices traders charge when you buy items. Their other pricing rules still apply.
logic: Higher makes buying more expensive; lower makes it cheaper. Each trader still applies their own pricing rules.
interaction: Item Values changes underlying prices; Prices Traders Pay applies when you sell instead.

label: Minimum Sellable Condition
rationale: Sets the lowest weapon or armor condition that traders will accept from you.
logic: 0% lets traders buy completely broken weapons and armor. 40% keeps vanilla. Higher settings make traders refuse more damaged gear.
interaction: Only decides whether a trader accepts damaged gear. The price they pay still depends on its condition and other trader rules.

label: Broken Gear Value
rationale: Sets how much value a fully broken item keeps. Higher means damaged gear is worth more.
logic: At the normal 10% setting, completely broken gear keeps 10% of its base value. Raising this makes badly damaged gear worth more.
interaction: Traders still apply their buy and sell prices. This only changes how durability affects an item's underlying value.

label: Trader Ammo Supply
rationale: Changes how much ammo traders carry. It does not unlock new ammo types.
logic: 1x keeps vanilla trader ammo stock. Lower settings reduce how much ammo traders carry; higher settings increase it.
interaction: Changes amount only. It does not add ammo types, alter availability chance, bypass player-rank progression, or change refresh timing.

label: Medic Supplies
rationale: Changes how many medical supplies medics sell. Item availability is separate.
logic: 100% keeps vanilla medic stock. Lower settings reduce stock; higher settings increase it.
interaction: Affects medic supplies only. Other traders, progression requirements, availability, and restock timing stay vanilla.

label: Item Values
rationale: Adjusts base values for food, medicine, ammo, armor, weapons, artifacts and mutant parts. Trader pricing still applies.

label: Guide Travel Fees
rationale: Makes guide travel cheaper or more expensive while preserving differences between routes.
logic: 100% keeps vanilla guide prices. 50% halves paid routes, 200% doubles them, and 0% makes paid routes free.
interaction: Guide discounts and other travel pricing rules still apply. This setting changes the route's starting fee.

label: Upgrade Cost
rationale: Makes gear upgrades cheaper or more expensive without changing which upgrades are available.
interaction: Each upgrade still has its own base price. This setting makes upgrades generally cheaper or more expensive without changing their relative costs.

label: Base Repair Cost
rationale: Changes basic repair costs. Your reputation with the technician's faction can change the final price.
interaction: Reputation-based repair prices still apply and can further raise or lower the final repair bill.

label: Hostile Repair Price
rationale: Changes repair costs when a technician's faction is hostile to you.
logic: Higher means more expensive repairs from hostile technicians; lower means cheaper repairs at this reputation level.
interaction: Base Repair Cost and the faction's current attitude both affect the final price.

label: Disliked Repair Price
rationale: Changes repair costs when a technician's faction dislikes you.
logic: Higher means more expensive repairs from disliked technicians; lower means cheaper repairs at this reputation level.
interaction: Base Repair Cost and the faction's current attitude both affect the final price.

label: Neutral Repair Price
rationale: Changes repair costs when your reputation with a technician's faction is neutral.
logic: Higher means more expensive repairs from neutral technicians; lower means cheaper repairs at this reputation level.
interaction: Base Repair Cost and the faction's current attitude both affect the final price.

label: Friendly Repair Price
rationale: Changes repair costs when a technician's faction is friendly to you.
logic: Higher means more expensive repairs from friendly technicians; lower means cheaper repairs at this reputation level.
interaction: Base Repair Cost and the faction's current attitude both affect the final price.

label: Main Quest Coupons
rationale: Changes coupon payouts from main quests. Side quests and stash rewards are separate.
interaction: Side Quest Coupons are adjusted independently. This does not change stash rewards or starting money.

label: Side Quest Coupons
rationale: Changes coupon payouts from side quests. Main quests and stash rewards are separate.
interaction: Main Quest Coupons are adjusted independently. This does not change stash rewards or starting money.

label: Armor Durability
rationale: Changes how quickly your armor loses condition. It does not change how much damage armor blocks.
interaction: Changes armor condition durability only. It does not change armor protection values, weapon wear or jamming thresholds.

label: Ammo Weight
rationale: Makes ammunition heavier or lighter in your inventory, keeping differences between ammo types.
interaction: Carry-capacity and encumbrance controls remain separate. This changes item Weight itself, so existing inventory-weight rules continue to apply normally.

label: Consumable Weight
rationale: Makes food and medical supplies heavier or lighter without changing their effects.
interaction: This does not change consumable effect strength or duration. DLC1 dry-ration weight is patched only when DLC1 is installed.

label: Global Anomaly Damage
rationale: Scales damage from all supported harmful anomalies. Individual anomaly damage still matters.
logic: Higher raises the global damage multiplier; lower reduces it. Individual anomaly damage settings still apply.
interaction: Individual anomaly damage and this global setting combine before armor and other protection.

label: Master Starvation Penalties
rationale: Enables Master's extra starvation penalties on top of ordinary hunger.
logic: When the game reaches its severe-hunger state, this bundle adds +200% stamina drain, periodic 4 HP starvation damage on a 10-second interval after its delay, and -100% health regeneration. OFF leaves only the normal hunger effects.
interaction: The game keeps the vanilla starvation activation point. The child controls only change stamina drain, damage, interval, delay and health-recovery strength.

label: Radiation Stamina Penalty
rationale: Enables Master's extra stamina penalty during heavy radiation. Radiation HP damage stays separate.
logic: When the game enters the heavy-radiation state used by this Master bundle, it adds an extra stamina-drain penalty (50% in vanilla). The normal radiation system remains active either way.
interaction: The activation point stays vanilla. Radiation Accumulation and Radiation Recovery determine how quickly the player reaches and leaves that state.

label: Master Severe-Fatigue Penalties
rationale: Enables Master's extra penalties for severe fatigue. Normal fatigue effects stay separate.
logic: When the game enters the Master severe-fatigue state, this bundle adds -20% maximum stamina, -20% carry capacity, +55% recoil, extra aim sway and shot spread in vanilla.
interaction: The activation point stays vanilla. The child controls only change how strong each severe-fatigue penalty becomes.

label: Well-Fed Stamina Recovery Bonus
rationale: Changes the stamina recovery bonus you get while well fed. It does not change when hunger starts.
logic: Higher values reward staying well fed with stronger stamina recovery; zero removes the bonus. The supported UI range does not turn this lowest-hunger state into a penalty.
interaction: The game keeps the vanilla boundary for leaving the well-fed state. Stamina Regen in the Stamina tab sets the underlying regeneration rate.

label: Starvation Action Cost
rationale: Makes actions cost more stamina while Master's starvation effect is active. This is not passive drain.
logic: 100% means +100% extra stamina cost, not normal cost. 0% removes this extra starvation cost.
interaction: Severe hunger also slows stamina recovery. This changes the extra cost of actions, not an ongoing drain.

label: Starvation Damage
rationale: Changes the HP lost each time Master's starvation damage hits.
logic: Higher values increase each starvation-damage charge; zero retains the bundle but removes direct HP damage from this component.
interaction: Starvation Damage Interval controls how often the charge repeats, while Starvation Penalty Delay controls when this effect begins after activation.

label: Starvation Damage Interval
rationale: Sets the time between starvation damage ticks while the Master effect is active.
logic: Lower values make the same damage arrive more frequently; higher values spread the damage out over a longer interval.
interaction: Practical starvation pressure depends on both this interval and Starvation Damage.

label: Starvation Penalty Delay
rationale: Changes how long Master's starvation penalties wait before taking effect.
logic: Lower values make the penalties engage sooner after the starvation state activates; higher values provide a longer grace period.
interaction: Master Starvation Penalties decides whether this bundle exists. This control only changes the grace period before its active penalties begin.

label: Starvation Health Recovery Penalty
rationale: Reduces HP recovery while Master's starvation effect is active.
logic: Higher values suppress health regeneration more strongly; zero removes this component.
interaction: This acts on regeneration rather than direct damage, so it combines with Starvation Damage and the Health tab regeneration settings.

label: Light Fatigue Aim Delay
rationale: Changes how much light fatigue slows aiming. Higher makes it take longer to aim.
logic: Higher values make aiming settle more slowly once the low-fatigue threshold is crossed; zero removes this standard low-fatigue aiming penalty.
interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla low-fatigue state.

label: Medium Fatigue Aim Delay
rationale: Changes how much moderate fatigue slows aiming. Higher makes it take longer to aim.
logic: Higher values further slow aiming during medium fatigue; zero removes this component.
interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla medium-fatigue state, replacing the low-state aiming penalty.

label: Severe Fatigue Aim Delay
rationale: Changes how much severe fatigue slows aiming. Higher makes it take longer to aim.
logic: Higher values make severe fatigue more disruptive to aiming; zero removes this standard aiming-time component.
interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla severe-fatigue state.

label: Medium Fatigue Reload Delay
rationale: Changes how much moderate fatigue slows reloading. Aiming penalties are separate.
logic: Higher values lengthen reloads more while medium fatigue is active; zero removes this penalty.
interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla medium-fatigue state. It is separate from the aiming-time penalty.

label: Severe Fatigue Reload Delay
rationale: Changes how much severe fatigue slows reloading. Master fatigue can add extra penalties.
logic: Higher values make reloads slower while severely fatigued. Zero removes this reload penalty.
interaction: Applies whenever the game is in its vanilla severe-fatigue state. Master Severe-Fatigue Penalties can add another layer on top.

label: Sleep HP Restore
rationale: Sets how much HP you regain after normal sleep. This tool defaults to 100 HP, unlike the game's original 300 HP.
logic: The editor's 1x means 100 HP restored on waking (0–200 HP range). The game's original value was 300 HP, so a reset returns to this tool's 100 HP default.
interaction: Medkits and passive HP regeneration remain separate.

label: Sleep Stamina Restore
rationale: Changes how much stamina normal sleep restores when you wake up. Passive stamina recovery is separate.
interaction: This affects the post-sleep restore, not passive stamina regeneration or action costs.

label: Severe Fatigue Stamina Loss
rationale: Reduces maximum stamina while Master's severe-fatigue effect is active.
logic: Higher values reduce the available stamina pool further; zero removes this component.
interaction: Max Stamina defines your normal pool; this loss applies only during Master severe fatigue.

label: Severe Fatigue Carry Loss
rationale: Reduces how much you can carry while Master's severe-fatigue effect is active.
logic: Higher values make fatigue reduce carrying capability more strongly; zero removes both carry-related components together.
interaction: Your normal carrying limit and equipment carry bonuses remain separate.

label: Severe Fatigue Recoil
rationale: Increases weapon recoil during Master's severe-fatigue effect.
interaction: This stacks with other recoil sources but does not change reload or aim-time penalties.

label: Severe-Fatigue Aim Sway
rationale: Makes your aim sway more during Master's severe-fatigue effect.
interaction: Recoil and bullet spread are separate penalties in the same Master fatigue bundle.

label: Severe Fatigue Bullet Spread
rationale: Makes shots spread wider during Master's severe-fatigue effect.
interaction: Recoil and aim sway are separate penalties in the same Master fatigue bundle.

label: Master Radiation Stamina Cost Increase
rationale: Makes actions cost more stamina during Master's heavy-radiation effect, without passive drain.
logic: 50% means +50% extra stamina cost. 0% removes this extra radiation cost.

label: Low Bleeding Damage
rationale: Changes HP lost with each damage tick during light bleeding. The time spent bleeding is separate.
interaction: Applies while the game is in its vanilla low-bleeding state. Natural Bleeding Recovery determines how long bleeding lasts.

label: Medium Bleeding Damage
rationale: Changes HP lost with each damage tick during moderate bleeding. The time spent bleeding is separate.
interaction: Applies while the game is in its vanilla medium-bleeding state. Movement and sleep penalties remain separate.

label: Severe Bleeding Damage
rationale: Changes HP lost with each damage tick during severe bleeding. The time spent bleeding is separate.
interaction: Applies while the game is in its vanilla severe-bleeding state. Bleeding Effect Strength can further change how dangerous bleeding feels overall.

label: Master Consumable Effect Penalties
rationale: Enables Master's weaker medical healing, plus other bundled consumable penalties.
logic: OFF leaves these extra Master penalties inactive. ON applies the Master-only changes on top of the normal item effects.
interaction: The healing controls directly below only matter while this switch is ON. Some food, energy-drink and Weird Kettle changes are still part of the same switch and are not individually adjustable yet.

label: Damage by Anomaly
rationale: Changes damage separately for each supported anomaly. The global anomaly setting adds another layer.
interaction: Use Global Anomaly Damage when you want to make all damaging anomalies stronger or weaker at once.

label: Flycatcher Movement Speed
rationale: Controls how fast you can move inside a Flycatcher anomaly. 100% keeps normal movement speed.
logic: Vanilla applies a -50% velocity change, so 50% of normal movement speed remains. 100% means no movement slowdown; 0% corresponds to a -100% velocity change.
interaction: Changes only player movement slowdown inside the Flycatcher. Projectile slowdown, HP/stamina regeneration penalties and turn slowdown remain separate.

label: Flycatcher Turn Speed
rationale: Controls how fast you can turn inside a Flycatcher anomaly. 100% keeps normal turning speed.
logic: Vanilla applies -0.7 to both yaw and pitch turn-rate effects, leaving 30% of normal turn speed. 100% means no turn slowdown; 0% corresponds to -1.0 on both effects.
interaction: The same setting is applied to Flycatcher yaw and pitch so horizontal and vertical looking stay synchronized. Movement speed is controlled separately.

label: Glass Shards Bleeding
rationale: Changes bleeding caused by Glass Shards without changing the anomaly's direct HP damage.
logic: 100% keeps vanilla Glass Shards bleeding. 0% removes it; 200% doubles it.
interaction: Glass Shards Health Damage is independent. Movement-speed thresholds and corrosion values remain vanilla.

label: Psy Drain Strength
rationale: Changes how strongly Psy anomalies affect your Psy meter. Other Psy effects are separate.
logic: 100% keeps vanilla Psy intensity. 0% removes this Psy effect; 200% doubles its strength.
interaction: Changes the continuous Psy drain only. Other Psy effects and thresholds remain unchanged.

label: Mutant Part Drop Chances
rationale: Sets the chance to find one mutant part after an eligible kill. Each mutant family has its own setting.

label: Bloodsucker Part Chance
rationale: Changes the chance of finding one Bloodsucker part after an eligible kill. It doesn't change mutant spawns.

rationale: Changes the chance of finding one Pseudogiant part after an eligible kill. It doesn't change mutant spawns.

rationale: Changes the chance of finding one Tushkan part after an eligible kill. It doesn't change mutant spawns.

label: Snork Part Chance
rationale: Changes the chance of finding one Snork part after an eligible kill. It doesn't change mutant spawns.

label: Weapon Wear per Shot
rationale: Changes how quickly your weapons lose condition when fired. Weapon jamming is separate.
logic: 100% keeps vanilla wear. 50% roughly halves condition loss per shot. 200% roughly doubles it.
interaction: Weapon Jam Rate is separate. Slower wear indirectly delays condition-related jams because your gun stays healthy longer.

label: Ammo Boxes Removed
rationale: Controls how many eligible world loot pickups are removed when you build the mod. Zero keeps them all.
interaction: This radar targets supported exploration loot categories, not quest or story rewards.

label: World Weapon Shuffle
rationale: Shuffles regular world weapons between suitable pickup spots when building. Pistols and main weapons stay in their own slots.
logic: OFF keeps vanilla weapon placement. ON reshuffles compatible world weapons. World Weapon Density decides how many weapon locations remain occupied.
interaction: World Weapon Density changes both location density and the guaranteed minimum copies of each of the 36 regular weapons.

label: World Weapon Density
rationale: Controls how many eligible world weapon spots stay filled after shuffling. All supported regular models remain represented.
logic: Higher density leaves more world weapon locations populated; lower density makes found weapons scarcer. Every regular weapon model is still kept in the pool.
interaction: Only shuffled regular weapons use this density; quest and unique weapon placements remain separate.

label: World Attachment Shuffle
rationale: Shuffles eligible world attachments between suitable spots without adding extra copies.
logic: OFF keeps vanilla attachment placement. ON reshuffles world attachments across compatible locations without changing how many exist.
interaction: Weapon and blueprint shuffles remain independent.

label: Remove World Detectors
rationale: Removes eligible non-quest detector pickups from the world. Quest and trader detectors stay untouched.
logic: OFF keeps vanilla detector placement. ON removes supported non-quest detector pickups from the world while leaving quest detectors alone.
interaction: Quest detectors and trader supplies stay untouched.

label: Blueprint Shuffle
rationale: Shuffles eligible world blueprint locations when building. Quest blueprints and total counts stay unchanged.
logic: OFF keeps vanilla blueprint locations. ON reshuffles the supported world blueprints so each build gives you a fresh layout with no duplicates.
interaction: Quest blueprint placements and total eligible blueprint counts remain unchanged.

label: Human Squad Size
rationale: Controls the maximum size of human squads for each player rank. Respawn frequency is separate.

label: Mutant Group Size
rationale: Controls group sizes of supported mutant species. It does not increase respawn frequency.
